children: A severe poultry disease in the world’s largest chicken exporter is weighing on shares of Tyson Foods

According to a statement from Brazil’s Minister of Agriculture Andre de Paula, a new case of Newcastle disease was identified at a commercial turkey plant in Santa Catarina. The region is Brazil’s second-largest supplier of chicken.
The viral disease affects the respiratory, nervous, and digestive systems of poultry. The ministry subsequently closed the impacted facility and suspended the further movement of poultry.
While the U.S. imports very little poultry from Brazil (less than $1M across all poultry categories), the news weighed on shares of U.S. poultry processors with Tyson Foods
down a little over 1%, JBS N.V.
down 2.6%, and shares in Brazil’s MBRF Global Foods

title: Poultry stocks rattled as Newcastle disease detected in Brazil
